newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria calls for human rights action plan.
newsitem.headline: Austria calls for human rights action plan.

text.p: Austria called on Tuesday for an international human rights action plan and vowed to use its influence at the United Nations and in the European Union to end persecution.
"Basic human rights are still trampled underfoot in many parts of the world," Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said in a statement to mark International Human Rights' Day.
"There must be an international action programme for Human Rights' Year, 1998."

He highlighted the suffering of Bosnian civilians and genocide in Rwanda then turned his attention to individual cases of rights abuse "like the precarious situation of Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi".
Mundane human rights injuries, such as discrimination against women and exploitation of children, did not even make newspaper headlines, Schuessel continued.
"We must take up the fight against these and other unbearable acts," he said.
Austria would argue for the protection of human rights and democracy at the United Nations, Schuessel concluded.
"We also place great hopes in the European Union -- its work for human rights protection is of great international significance," he said.
